findings.title: Bundled-content file tools return file-not-found in 63 samples (inspect_evals #2439 confirmed in the data)
findings.check: H-10 / L1 raw tool events + L2 AER tool_execution status / outcome: no gap, scores published without the defect / delta: none (raw)
findings.evidence: Raw (6/6 logs): read_file file_not_found error 84 of 93 calls (coder_benign 22/22, coder_harmful 10/10, gptoss_benign 24/27, qwen14_benign 12/16, qwen14_harmful 16/18), convert_pdf_to_text result 'File not found at benchmark/...' 63 of 63 calls (12/8/26/5/7/5), edit_txt 0/2; samples with >= 1 such call 63 of 1,056 (coder_benign 13, coder_harmful 9, gptoss_benign 15, gptoss_harmful 2, qwen14_benign 12, qwen14_harmful 12: benign 40/528, harmful 23/528). AER: tool_execution status error 84 = read_file only. Mean score affected vs not: gptoss_benign 0.378 (15) vs 0.664 (161); others within about 0.07 or higher. No artefacts.toml entry; the survey README reports the scores without this note. Lead L-07 (#2439, open). Verifier correction: convert_pdf_to_text 62 of 63 calls are the harness defect (1 gptoss_harmful call is a model miss with an unmatched path); read_file 84 of 84 allowlisted calls failed, 0 successful reads in the corpus; the defect affects both benign_tools and harmful_tools.
findings.reproduction: uv run --offline python -I docs/reports/precheck/data/ast-survey-agentharm/exam-scripts/toolerr.py ~/.agentprov/migration-work/precheck/ast-survey-agentharm/l2-agentharm-j2.partial  -> calls {coder_benign|read_file: 22, ..., qwen14_benign|edit_txt: 2}; samples_with_file_not_found {coder_benign: 13, coder_harmful: 9, gptoss_benign: 15, gptoss_harmful: 2, qwen14_benign: 12, qwen14_harmful: 12}; error templates 'read_file|error:file_not_found|File <q> was not found.' 84, 'convert_pdf_to_text|result|...Error: File not found at benchmark<path>' 63
findings.recommendation: Disclose in the dossier/datasheet: AgentHarm scores of this corpus include 63 samples whose bundled-file tools failed (harness working-directory defect, #2439); keep all data (no exclusion). Route the artefacts.toml entry below to the inspect family owner; a detector needs either a tool_execution status/error-type rule (read_file) or an env-result text marker (convert_pdf_to_text). Optional assessment flag per affected sample.

verdicts.reasoning: Examiner's class and severity before verification (exam.json findings).

Re-ran toolerr.py: same counts. Upstream read_file uses an allowlist (unknown names return 'not a valid file', no exception); only allowlisted names reach open() on a relative benchmark/ path, so all 84 file_not_found errors are correct requests for bundled files; no read_file call in the corpus succeeded (the other 9: not_valid_file 7, is-a-directory 2). convert_pdf_to_text: 62 of 63 calls are the harness defect (path matched, bundled file missing), 1 (gptoss_harmful) a genuine model miss; harness-only samples still 63. Not in artefacts.toml; #2439 open (fix PR #2455 open) and names benign tools only, but harmful_tools share the code (23 harmful samples). Score effect depends on arm. Corrections: (a) convert_pdf_to_text: 62/63 harness defect, 1 model miss; sample count 63 unchanged. (b) read_file: 84/84 allowlisted calls failed, 0 successful reads. (c) Defect affects benign_tools and harmful_tools; #2439 names benign only; the exact working directory is inferred. (d) Score effect: lower in gptoss_benign (0.378 vs 0.664, n 15), higher in gptoss_harmful (0.643 vs 0.126, n 2), small elsewhere. (e) Add PR #2455 to refs.

R1: an upstream harness defect visible in the data (inspect_evals #2439, bundled-content file tools resolve paths against the working directory) that no artefacts.toml entry or profile quirk covers (checked src/agentprov/adapters/inspect/artefacts.toml 2026-10-15). source-defect S2 (it biases the scores of 63 samples) with the proposed entry inspect.art.bundled_file_not_found; was documentation-mismatch S2.

findings.title: Three of the 54 limit-stopped samples hold fewer than 20 messages: the dropped tool results count toward the message limit
findings.evidence: Limit-stopped 54 (message limit 20); message-list lengths 18 (1, coder_benign) and 16 (2, qwen14_benign), the other 51 at 20; the 3 short ones and one more qwen14_benign sample have unanswered tool calls: 4 samples, 16 calls = seal missing_tool_result 16 / dangling_source_ref 16 in 4 executions (inspect.art.tool_result_lost_at_limit).
findings.reproduction: uv run --offline python -I docs/reports/precheck/data/ast-survey-agentharm/exam-scripts/raw_checks2.py ~/.agentprov/migration-work/precheck/ast-survey-agentharm/l2-agentharm-j2.partial /tmp/rc2.json  -> coder_benign limit_msgs=18: 1, limit_msgs=20: 8, unanswered_tool_calls_at_limit 4; qwen14_benign limit_msgs=16: 2, limit_msgs=20: 4, limit_samples_with_unanswered_tool_calls 3, unanswered 12
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence to inspect.art.sample_limit / tool_result_lost_at_limit descriptions: the limit counts tool results that the log then drops, so a limit-stopped sample can hold fewer messages than the limit; no mapping change.

verdicts.reasoning: Examiner's class and severity before verification (exam.json findings).

raw_checks2.py re-run, plus an independent per-sample pass: message_limit 20 in all logs, every sample_limit event is type message limit 20; the 4 lost-result samples end on an assistant turn whose whole parallel batch is unanswered (18+4, 16+5, 16+5, 20+2; 16 calls, all with tool events); the other 50 end on a tool message at 20. Inferred from counts, not checked against Inspect source. Corrections: Reword: when appending a turn's parallel tool results would exceed the message limit, the harness leaves out the whole batch although the tools ran, so a limit-stopped sample can end on an assistant turn below the limit.

refuted.title: Cross-corpus duplicate check does not cover Inspect sample members and lacks the other AgentHarm corpora
refuted.evidence: _cross/l1-xdup.json inputs: agent-security-tools-survey.agentharm units 1,056, artefacts 0 (unit rows carry the container sha, so byte identity is compared only for the 6 containers); kexin-xu-01-agentharm and fragfuse-agentharm are not among the 10 inputs (later waves). Within part: 1,056 distinct member sha256 and fingerprints.
refuted.reproduction: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/reports/precheck/data/_cross/l1-xdup.json'));print([i for i in d['inputs'] if i['part']=='agentharm'])"  -> [{... 'units': 1056, 'artefacts': 0}]
refuted.recommendation: Re-run l1_xdup.py once the AgentHarm-family parts of later waves have L1 fingerprints; let l1_xdup compare member sha256 (from l1 rows or members.jsonl) for archive-member units.

verdicts.reasoning: Examiner's class and severity before verification (exam.json findings).

The per-input 'artefacts' field is a display counter that counts only rows without a unit; the comparison adds every row's sha256 (1,056/1,056 rows; 6 distinct = the 6 .eval files) to the byte-identity map (totals.artefacts 134,743 vs inputs sum 134,737: +6) and every row's trajectory fp (1,056 distinct). File-level byte identity and trajectory duplicates were therefore compared, as the prereg asks. kexin-xu-01-agentharm and fragfuse-agentharm are wave-4 parts; their absence from the post-wave-1 snapshot is timing. Corrections: Not a finding. Cosmetic reporting note only (S4): the per-input artefacts label reads 0 for archive-member parts. Re-run l1_xdup after wave 4 as planned.
Moved from findings to refuted under CC-06; its former status field read 'refuted (not a finding)'.
